headline: RBI raises minimum daily CRR maintenance from 90% to 99% from fortnight of Oct 16, 2026
summary_points: RBI has raised the minimum daily CRR maintenance requirement for scheduled banks under Section 42(1) of the RBI Act, 1934.
The change follows a review of current liquidity conditions.
The average of daily CRR maintained must still not fall below the CRR prescribed by RBI over the reporting fortnight.

rows: Minimum daily CRR maintenance (as % of required CRR)

who_is_affected: All scheduled banks, which now have much less room to run daily CRR balances below the required level.
action_required: Banks should align their treasury and liquidity management so that daily CRR balances stay at or above 99% of the requirement from the fortnight beginning October 16, 2026.

social.linkedin:
RBI has tightened the daily Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) maintenance norm for scheduled banks.

Under Section 42(1) of the RBI Act, 1934, banks could so far maintain at least 90% of the required CRR on all days of the reporting fortnight, as long as the daily average met the prescribed CRR.

Vide circular RBI/2026-27/290 dated October 9, 2026, the minimum daily maintenance has been raised from 90% to 99% of the requirement, following a review of current liquidity conditions.

Effective date: fortnight beginning October 16, 2026.

What it means: banks will have far less flexibility to manage day-to-day CRR balances, and treasury teams will need to plan daily liquidity more closely. The fortnightly average requirement remains unchanged.

Please verify the details with the official RBI circular before acting.
